title: Weekday-conditioned number inclusion model

hypothesis.question: Does weekday-conditioned number frequency improve the ex-ante probability of a 5-number set beyond global-frequency and uniform baselines?
hypothesis.null: Conditional on the five-of-forty design, weekday does not add stable information beyond global number frequency.
hypothesis.alternative: A fixed hierarchical weekday effect improves proper joint log score and marginal inclusion Brier score on future targets.
baselines: M1 global-frequency weighted fixed-size subset model, beta=200
hypothesis.candidate_model: M7 weekday-conditioned weighted fixed-size subset model.

fixed_design.alpha_selection: Choose alpha minimizing Validation mean joint log-loss; exact ties choose the larger alpha. No Blind OOS access during selection.
fixed_design.training_rule: For each target, all counts use only draws strictly earlier than that target. Validation outcomes may enter later validation prefixes; Blind OOS outcomes may enter later Blind OOS prefixes, but alpha remains frozen.
fixed_design.weekday_rule: UTC weekday derived from ISO target date; no future calendar or outcome fields used.
metrics: joint negative log probability of observed five-number subset
mean Brier score across 40 marginal inclusion probabilities

inference.correction: Holm step-down across the four Blind OOS endpoints.

integrity_tests: sum of marginal inclusion probabilities equals 5

prospective_freeze.rule: Research-only add-on; do not modify existing global/positional freezes or Q60.

guardrails: Historical Blind OOS is not a virgin holdout because the archive has been examined in earlier SONAR research.
No production engine change, promotion, or automatic merge.
Q60 exact-number provenance for contest 314 remains unresolved until an official exact-number source is available; do not advance the gate from this experiment.
